title: The Stilt Market Over the Tar Lake
story: A mudlark pup has slipped into the sticky tar lake, and the only rope for leagues hangs at Tarquill's crooked stall on stilts. The long-legged merchant grins and taps his sign: three coils will reach the pup, but nothing at his stall has a simple price. Mr 6 counts on his fingers — all six of them — and smiles back.
question: One coil of rope costs 40 amber drams. Tarquill adds a 25% stilt tax to the total, and then takes 10% off that taxed total as a 'quick-foot discount.' How many amber drams does Mr 6 pay for 3 coils?
solution: Three coils at plain price cost 3 × 40 = 120 amber drams.
The 25% stilt tax raises it: 120 × 1.25 = 150 amber drams.
The 10% discount takes 15 off: 150 × 0.90 = 135 amber drams.
praise: Starting with the plain price of 120 was exactly the right first move — the tax and the discount just each needed their own separate step.
hint: Do one change at a time: plain price for 3 coils first, then grow it by the tax, then shrink that new total by the discount.
victory: Mr 6 counts out 135 drams precisely, and Tarquill's grin collapses because nobody ever catches both steps. The rope flies, the mudlark pup is hauled out tar-sticky and delighted, and Mr 6 walks home wearing a free (if gooey) hug.
imagePrompt: A lanky stilt-legged merchant monster with a crooked price sign leaning over a rickety plank stall above a glossy black tar lake at dusk, while a small brave numeral-six knight in a blue cape counts coins and a muddy pup flails below.
